themes_detail.label: Street noise explosion
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from streets and sidewalks spiked to 56 this week—a 307% jump from the 13.8-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—suggesting a sudden shift in outdoor activity, construction, or street conditions in Midwood that warrants investigation.
evidence: 56 street/sidewalk noise complaints this week vs. 13.8 weekly average (307% spike, z-score 6.95)
Statistically significant spike occurred within the last 7 days
No prior sustained pattern of street noise complaints in 90-day volume data
reporting_angles: Are new outdoor dining sheds, street fairs, or nightlife venues recently operating in the district?
Has street construction, delivery schedules, or refuse collection changed this week?

themes_detail.label: Construction and plumbing surge
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints jumped to 42 this week—a 239% increase from the 12.4-complaint weekly average—potentially signaling a coordinated wave of renovation work, infrastructure projects, or building violations across Midwood.
evidence: 42 construction/plumbing complaints this week vs. 12.4 weekly average (239% spike, z-score 7.59)
303 DOB building permits filed in the last 90 days (226 alterations, 31 new buildings, 8 full demolitions)
Spike occurred this week; no prior sustained pattern in baseline data
reporting_angles: Which DOB permits filed recently correspond to the construction complaints this week?
Are plumbing complaints linked to aging infrastructure in specific blocks, or scattered across the district?

themes_detail.label: Encampment emergence
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints appeared at 3 this week—a 2300% spike from a near-zero baseline of 0.1 complaints weekly over 8 weeks—marking a sudden and unprecedented arrival of unsheltered populations or informal housing in Midwood that requires immediate neighborhood context.
evidence: 3 encampment complaints this week vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike, z-score 8.69)
Highest z-score among all spikes, indicating extreme statistical deviation
No prior mentions of encampments in 90-day complaint history
reporting_angles: Where are the encampments located? Are they concentrated near transit, parks, or commercial areas?
What triggered the sudden emergence—did a shelter close, or did a policy change push populations into the district?

themes_detail.label: Non-emergency police surge
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police complaints jumped to 12 last week—a 357% increase from the 2.6-complaint weekly average—indicating a rise in quality-of-life disturbances or low-level disorder that may reflect broader safety or behavioral shifts in the district.
evidence: 12 non-emergency police complaints last week vs. 2.6 weekly average (357% spike, z-score 8.44)
Spike occurred last week; timeframe suggests an emerging trend rather than a one-off incident
No contextualization available on complaint types (disorderly conduct, trespassing, etc.)
reporting_angles: What specific behaviors or incidents are triggering non-emergency police calls? Are they linked to encampment emergence or street activity?
Are complaints concentrated in specific neighborhoods (near schools, parks, transit hubs) or scattered?

themes_detail.label: Rezoning pipeline activity
themes_detail.summary: Five active land-use applications are under review in Midwood (including the 1455 Coney Island Avenue and 2586 Nostrand Avenue rezonings currently in agency review), alongside two historic district designations, signaling potential neighborhood-scale development pressure and property owner concerns worth monitoring.
evidence: Five active ULURP and Non-ULURP applications in various review stages
Two historic district designations (Ditmas Park West, Beverley Square West) in City Council review
Three rezoning applications (Coney Island Ave, Nostrand Ave, Flatbush Ave) in early to mid-stage review
reporting_angles: What do the rezoning applications propose? Who benefits and who opposes them?
Are the historic district designations intended to block or guide development in the face of rezoning pressure?
